Thanks for the tag, Lauren. Sarah — copied a short playbook below and a proposed set of targeted redlines (see attached). I'm keeping the language pragmatic to move the commercial discussion forward; if Acme needs broader protection we can escalate but we'll want to trade for other concessions (e.g., higher fees or different SLA commitments).

Claims Playbook (summary):
1) Trigger: Redwood will indemnify Customer for third-party claims that the Service as delivered infringes a third party's intellectual property rights, provided Customer promptly notifies Redwood in writing and (if requested) cooperates in the defense.
2) Defense Control: Redwood will assume defense with counsel of our choosing; Redwood will consult with Customer on material strategy and will not settle any claim that imposes obligations on Customer without Customer's prior written consent.
3) Exclusions: No indemnity for (a) content generated by Customer prompts that incorporate customer's proprietary third-party code or data; (b) open-source license compliance claims (we propose mutual carveouts and remediation cooperation); (c) claims arising from Customer's modification of the Service.
4) Remedies & Cap: Redwood proposes liability limited to direct damages, with an aggregate cap equal to fees paid in the prior 12 months under the applicable Order Form. Willful misconduct and fraud excluded from cap.
5) Procedure: Notice, cooperation, allowance of defense control, and settlement approval (standard defense control flow).

Suggested clause snippet (for MSA §X.Y):
"Supplier shall defend, indemnify and hold Customer harmless from and against any third-party claim alleging that the Supplier's Service, when used as permitted hereunder, infringes such third party's intellectual property rights. Supplier's obligation to indemnify is conditioned on Customer (a) providing prompt written notice of the claim to Supplier, (b) granting Supplier sole control of the defense and settlement of the claim, and (c) cooperating with Supplier in the defense. Supplier shall not enter any settlement that (i) imposes any obligation or restriction on Customer, or (ii) admits fault on behalf of Customer, without Customer's prior written consent. Supplier's aggregate liability under this Section shall be limited to direct damages not to exceed the fees paid by Customer to Supplier under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."
Notes:
- For patent-heavy customers we can accept a carveout to include patent claims but ask for a higher cap or insurance (we've had success negotiating a 2x fee cap or offering IP indemnity with carrier-backed insurance for larger deals).
- We should not accept joint-and-several liability for punitive or third-party consequential damages.

Attachments: redline_MSA_ACME_v3.docx (tracked changes, docx)

I'll be available on Thursday at 3pm PT for the call if you want legal on.

Marissa — thank you for the clear playbook and suggested clause. A few quick points from Acme counsel:

1) Defense control: Acme typically requires joint defense rights for IP claims where Acme's confidential data or integration work is implicated. They're concerned about being excluded from settlement discussions.
2) Cap: Our procurement stance is that IP indemnity should not be limited to the equivalent 12 months fees for core infra services; they prefer a separate IP carveout or a higher cap (we proposed 2x ARR).
3) Open-source: We are open to a mutual carveout for open-source license compliance, but we need clarity on remediation responsibilities if the Service includes third-party OSS components.

We'll bring the points above to the Thursday sync. For transparency, Acme has one pending third-party patent claim from 2024 which is included in the claims log — they want to understand how Redwood would have handled a similar claim and whether Redwood would have taken control of defense earlier.

Regards,
Sarah

Adding a technical/legal note: for model-driven services we should be explicit that indemnity triggers exclude claims arising from Customer-provided prompts or Customer-supplied data that cause the Service to produce infringing output. Practically: if the Customer feeds in a competitor's source code and then claims infringement, Redwood shouldn't be on the hook.

Proposed compromise positions to propose on the call:
- Redwood offers IP indemnity for third-party claims arising from Supplier-delivered Service code and models, limited to direct damages and a cap equal to 2x the annualized fees (or insurance-backed arrangement for enterprise deals).
- Defense control: primary defense by Redwood with a right for Customer to participate; Redwood will not settle to bind Customer without written consent.
- Open-source: mutual carveout for license compliance; each party responsible for remediation of components they contributed.

These moves should address procurement's cap concerns while protecting Redwood's engineering and model exposure. Happy to present on the call.

-Rishi

Sarah — thanks for the candid feedback and for surfacing the patent from 2024. Per our internal discussion (Marissa & Rishi) here's the path forward ahead of the call: 

1) Draft compromise clause: Redwood will propose an IP indemnity limited to direct damages, with an adjustable cap — default: fees paid in prior 12 months, negotiable up to 2x ARR for enterprise-sized deals or where customer can substantiate material IP exposure.
2) Defense: Redwood will take primary control of defense; Customer may participate and Redwood will not bind Customer to any settlement without written consent. For claims implicating Customer-supplied confidential data or integrations, Redwood will afford Customer greater participation rights.
3) OSS: mutual carveout and remediation responsibility allocated to the contributor of the OSS component.

Next steps: I scheduled a 30-min negotiation call for Thursday 3:00pm PT (invite sent). Marissa and Rishi will join to walk legal through the compromise language and the MSA redline.
